title: Quasi-compact algebraic-space morphisms: base change and fppf descent
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale morphism from a quasi-compact scheme [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. A morphism $h:A\to B$ is quasi-compact if $A\times_BZ$ is a quasi-compact space for every quasi-compact algebraic space $Z$ with a map $Z\to B$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism of algebraic spaces. If $f$ is quasi-compact, then $X\times_YY'\to Y'$ is quasi-compact for every morphism $Y'\to Y$ of algebraic spaces [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $\{Y_i\to Y\}_{i\in I}$ be any small jointly surjective family on field-valued point classes [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family], each map being flat and locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Then $f$ is quasi-compact if and only if every $X\times_YY_i\to Y_i$ is quasi-compact. No separation or finite-type hypothesis on $f$ is imposed.

proof.text: Let $f$ be quasi-compact and let $Y^{\prime}\to Y$ be arbitrary. For any quasi-compact algebraic space $Z\to Y^{\prime}$, the universal property of the fibre products of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] identifies $(X\times_YY^{\prime})\times_{Y^{\prime}}Z$ with $X\times_YZ$: on test schemes both describe a pair of sections of $X$ and $Z$ with the same image in $Y$. The latter space is quasi-compact by the definition for $f$. Thus the base change is quasi-compact. This also proves the forward implication for the given family.

source.place: Tag 03HF (lemma-base-change-quasi-compact), omitted proof expanded by transitivity of fibre products

proof.text: For the converse assume each $f_i:X\times_YY_i\to Y_i$ quasi-compact. Fix any quasi-compact algebraic space $Z\to Y$ and put $P=X\times_YZ$ and $P_i=Y_i\times_YZ$. The quasi-compact scheme atlas in the definition of $Z$ gives a quasi-compact point space $|Z|$ by [lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas]. The cartesian-point surjectivity of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], together with the assumed joint surjectivity, shows that the images of the $|P_i|\to|Z|$ cover $|Z|$. For each $i$ choose the atlas $U_i=\coprod_{a\in A_i}U_{ia}\to P_i$ of [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover], with every $U_{ia}$ affine. Its point map is surjective and open. Hence the images of its open summands $|U_{ia}|$ are open in $|P_i|$ and cover it.

source.place: Tag 0DFQ (lemma-zariski-etale-smooth-syntomic-fppf-fpqc), proof choosing affine etale charts above a test space; Tag 03E4 (lemma-quasi-compact-space) for compactness of the point space

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-flat-lfp-space-universally-open] to each original map $Y_i\to Y$. Its conclusion makes $|P_i|\to|Z|$ open for this arbitrary algebraic-space base change; no flatness-descent or quasi-compactness of $Y_i\to Y$ is required. Consequently the images of the $|U_{ia}|\to|Z|$ are open and cover $|Z|$. The definition of topological quasi-compactness [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] gives finitely many of these charts, say $V_r=U_{i_ra_r}$ for $1\leq r\leq n$, whose images cover $|Z|$. The finite list is empty if $Z$ is empty. Each selected morphism $V_r\to Z$ still has its specified factorization through $Y_{i_r}$, via $P_{i_r}$. This is the finite-chart refinement in Tag 0DFQ, constructed here rather than assuming that joint surjectivity alone implies an fpqc cover.

source.place: Tag 0DFQ (lemma-zariski-etale-smooth-syntomic-fppf-fpqc), proof: open images and a finite subcover

proof.text: Each $V_r$ is a quasi-compact scheme by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; as an algebraic space it is quasi-compact using its identity etale atlas. The quasi-compactness of $f_{i_r}$ applied to $V_r\to Y_{i_r}$ therefore says that $T_r=(X\times_YY_{i_r})\times_{Y_{i_r}}V_r$ is quasi-compact. Transitivity of fibre products identifies $T_r$ with $P\times_ZV_r=X\times_YV_r$, respecting the projection to $P$. Each $|T_r|$ is quasi-compact by the quasi-compact-atlas implication in [lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas].

source.place: Tag 041L (lemma-descending-property-quasi-compact), proof: quasi-compact test charts give quasi-compact pulled-back sources

proof.text: By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], the image of $|T_r|\to|P|$ is the inverse image under $|P|\to|Z|$ of the image of $|V_r|\to|Z|$. Thus these finitely many images cover $|P|$, and all the maps $|T_r|\to|P|$ are continuous. Given any open cover of $|P|$, pull it back to each quasi-compact $|T_r|$, choose a finite subcover there, and take the union of the finitely many selected index sets. Since the images cover $|P|$, this finite union covers $|P|$. For $n=0$ the same image identity gives $|P|=\varnothing$. Therefore $|P|$ is quasi-compact. Apply [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas] to obtain an affine scheme etale-surjecting onto $P$; it is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so $P$ is quasi-compact in the definition of the item. Since $Z\to Y$ was any quasi-compact algebraic-space test, $f$ is quasi-compact.

lean.statement: theorem quasiCompact_baseChange_and_fppfLocal {S : Scheme.{u}} {X Y : AlgebraicSpace S} (f : X ⟶ Y) : (IsQuasiCompactPresheafMap f.hom.hom ↔ ∀ (Z : AlgebraicSpace S), (∃ (U : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ Z.obj.obj), CompactSpace U.left ∧ IsEtale a ∧ IsSurjective a) → ∀ g : Z ⟶ Y, ∃ (V : Over S) (b : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Limits.pullback f.hom.hom g.hom.hom), CompactSpace V.left ∧ IsEtale b ∧ IsSurjective b) ∧ (IsQuasiCompactPresheafMap f.hom.hom → ∀ (Y' : AlgebraicSpace S) (g : Y' ⟶ Y), IsQuasiCompactPresheafMap (Limits.pullback.snd f.hom.hom g.hom.hom)) ∧ (∀ (I : Type w) (Yᵢ : I → AlgebraicSpace S) (g : ∀ i : I, Yᵢ i ⟶ Y), (∀ i : I, MapIsFlat (g i)) → (∀ i : I, MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation (g i)) → IsJointlySurjective (fun i : I ↦ (g i).hom.hom) → (IsQuasiCompactPresheafMap f.hom.hom ↔ ∀ i : I, IsQuasiCompactPresheafMap (Limits.pullback.snd f.hom.hom (g i).hom.hom)))
lean.note: The first conjunct expands the node's all-quasi-compact-space-test definition and identifies it with the existing affine-test atlas predicate; no second quasi-compactness definition is introduced. The other two conjuncts give arbitrary algebraic-space base change and fppf locality for every small family, including the empty family. The sheaf fibre products are rendered by their canonical underlying presheaf pullbacks.
